findings.title: `source_bar_stamping` accepts raw strings and stores them unconverted
findings.description:
The check `self.source_bar_stamping not in SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` is a frozenset membership test. `TimeMeaning` is a `StrEnum` (`timestamps.py:37`). CPython defines `class StrEnum(str, ReprEnum)` (`enum.py:1310`), so `str` precedes `Enum` in the MRO and the member hashes and compares equal to its value. As a result, `Market(source_bar_stamping="period_start", ...)` passes validation and stores a plain `str`.

The other enum fields do not have this hole. `continuity_kind` (`markets.py:102-104`) and `session_mode` both go through `_require_instance`. A caller that later writes `market.source_bar_stamping is TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START` gets `False`. The canonical bytes are identical, so the hash does not reveal the problem. No test covers it: `REJECTED_MARKETS` only includes the enum member `AVAILABLE_AT` and a plain string for `continuity_kind`.

Fix: call `_require_instance(self.source_bar_stamping, TimeMeaning, ...)` before the membership check, and add a case with `"period_start"` to the rejection tests.

findings.title: Validation helpers are duplicated across `markets.py` and `instruments.py`
findings.description:
`_require_instance` is defined twice with the same body, once in `instruments.py:80-86` and once in `markets.py:132-138`. The only difference is the exception class. `Instrument.__post_init__` (`instruments.py:69-75`) also repeats the `_require_nonempty_str` logic from `markets.py:123-129` inline. Both copies annotate `expected: type` with a bare `type`. I could not confirm whether pyright strict flags that under `reportMissingTypeArgument`.

This breaks the project's DRY rule. Fix it with one validator module parameterized by error class, and let both modules import it. That module must stay free of `calendars`, `canonical`, and `fixtures` imports, which `test_import_boundary.py` enforces.

findings.title: Unbounded `Decimal` exponents can make `canonicalize` allocate about a gigabyte
findings.description:
`_require_positive_decimal` accepts any finite `Decimal` above zero. `Decimal("1E+999999999")` passes at line 98. `canonicalize` then calls `_decimal_plain_digits` (`canonical.py:104-109`), which pads with `"0" * exponent` for positive exponents and builds `"0." + "0" * ...` for very negative ones. One `tick_size` value would produce a string of about 10^9 characters before hashing.

Fix: bound the magnitude in the validator, for example by checking `value.adjusted()` against a named constant. Add a test with a large exponent. I reached this by reading the code, not by executing it.

findings.title: Market field annotations are narrower than what the constructor accepts
findings.description: The class docstring (`markets.py:74-75`) says `session_calendars` and `adjustment_bases` accept any iterable. The field annotations say `tuple` and `frozenset`. Pyright strict would flag a typed call that passes a list. Test helpers route arguments through `dict[str, Any]` (`test_markets.py:36-45`), so pyright never sees those calls. Either annotate the constructor input as an iterable or drop the "any iterable" promise.

findings.title: `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS` is defined but never used
findings.description: The constant is unused. The expected end values are written as literals instead.

findings.title: Uniformity test does not read per-market stamping
findings.description: Every row passes `TimeMeaning.PERIOD_START` to `period_end`, including the Kalshi instrument. That market declares `source_bar_stamping=TimeMeaning.PERIOD_END` (`fixtures/markets.py:54`). Nothing in `src` reads `source_bar_stamping` yet, so no tested path can observe the difference. The test does not claim otherwise, but a reader could take "one code path serves every market" to mean the per-market stamping is covered. When a consumer appears, the test should take the start meaning from the market.

findings.title: `test_calendars_are_referenced_by_id_only` is a weak test
findings.description: `replace(EQUITY_FIXTURE)` makes a copy with no changes, so the test is a no-op setup. The assertion checks only that one literal date string is absent. A positive check that the calendar id appears in the canonical bytes would test the intended property more directly.

findings.title: Test helper `make_market` is duplicated with different defaults
findings.description: `test_instruments.py:43` and `test_markets.py:36` each define a `make_market`, with different signatures and defaults. Consider one shared helper in a test `conftest.py`.

findings.title: ISO 4217 currency check rejects USDT, which conflicts with the planned crypto market
findings.description: `_CURRENCY_CODE` accepts exactly three uppercase letters. `test_instruments.py:97` asserts that `"USDT"` is rejected, so this was a deliberate choice. Crypto quote currencies such as USDT and USDC are common, and the project lists crypto as a later market. The project owner should confirm this rule before crypto work starts.

findings.title: Extended fixture calendar literals match their wall-clock comments
findings.description: I re-derived all nine extended session open and close values, plus the coverage bounds, from the wall times in the comments. The derivation used EDT (UTC-4) through Nov 1 and EST (UTC-5) after, with the epoch anchored at 2026-01-01. Every value matches. The longest extended session is 16 hours, under the 24-hour `MAX_TIME_BAR_WIDTH_NS` check in `calendars.py:246`. The uniformity test's expected ends also match the fixture opens plus 60 seconds for the equity, Globex, and always-open rows.

findings.title: Decimal identity is consistent with equality
findings.description: `_decimal_plain_digits` strips trailing zeros, so `Decimal("1")` and `Decimal("1.0")` produce identical canonical bytes. That matches their equality and hash, so `ContractTerms` identity does not split equal values. The exponent issue above is a separate matter of magnitude, not of equality.

structured_findings.summary: `source_bar_stamping` accepts raw strings and stores them unconverted
Validation helpers are duplicated across `markets.py` and `instruments.py`
Unbounded `Decimal` exponents can make `canonicalize` allocate about a gigabyte
Market field annotations are narrower than what the constructor accepts
Uniformity test does not read per-market stamping
Test helper `make_market` is duplicated with different defaults
ISO 4217 currency check rejects USDT, which conflicts with the planned crypto market
Extended fixture calendar literals match their wall-clock comments
Decimal identity is consistent with equality
